nodes.summary: If the Krylov vectors are linearly independent and $j + 1 < k$, then $T q_j = \sum_{i \le j+1} h_{ij}\, q_i$, the $j$-th column of $T Q_n = Q_{n+1} \tilde H_n$.
nodes.title: The Arnoldi relation

nodes.summary: The Arnoldi vectors $q_0, \dots, q_{k-1}$ are the normalized Gram–Schmidt vectors of the Krylov vectors $r, Tr, \dots, T^{k-1} r$; in exact arithmetic and without breakdown they are the vectors produced by the Arnoldi iteration.
nodes.title: Arnoldi vectors

nodes.summary: If $(q_i)$ is a finite orthonormal family and $x$ lies in its span, then $x = \sum_i \langle q_i, x \rangle\, q_i$.
nodes.title: Orthonormal expansion in a finite span

nodes.summary: If $T$ is symmetric (self-adjoint) and the Krylov vectors are linearly independent, then also $h_{ij} = 0$ for $j > i + 1$; together with the Hessenberg property, $H_k$ is tridiagonal and the Arnoldi iteration reduces to the three-term Lanczos recurrence.
nodes.title: Lanczos: for symmetric operators the Arnoldi matrix is tridiagonal

nodes.summary: If the Krylov vectors $r, Tr, \dots, T^{k-1} r$ are linearly independent, then $h_{ij} = \langle q_i, T q_j \rangle = 0$ whenever $i > j + 1$.
nodes.title: The Arnoldi matrix is upper Hessenberg

nodes.summary: The $k \times k$ matrix $H_k = Q_k^* T Q_k$ with entries $h_{ij} = \langle q_i, T q_j \rangle$, where $q_0, \dots, q_{k-1}$ are the Arnoldi vectors.
nodes.title: Arnoldi Hessenberg matrix

nodes.summary: If $(q_l)$ is orthonormal, $i \notin s$ and $x \in \operatorname{span}\{q_l : l \in s\}$, then $\langle q_i, x \rangle = 0$.
nodes.title: An orthonormal vector is orthogonal to the span of the others

nodes.summary: If the Krylov vectors are linearly independent, $H_k$ satisfies Mathlib's predicate `Matrix.IsUpperHessenberg`: all entries strictly below the first subdiagonal vanish.
nodes.title: The Arnoldi matrix is an upper Hessenberg matrix

nodes.summary: For a linear operator $T$ on an inner product space and a vector $r$, the Krylov vectors are $r, Tr, \dots, T^{k-1} r$.
nodes.title: Krylov vectors
The operator maps each Arnoldi vector into the next Krylov space

nodes.summary: If the Krylov vectors $r, Tr, \dots, T^{k-1} r$ are linearly independent, the Arnoldi vectors are orthonormal.
nodes.title: Arnoldi vectors are orthonormal

nodes.summary: For every $j < k$, $\operatorname{span}\{q_0, \dots, q_j\} = \operatorname{span}\{r, Tr, \dots, T^j r\} = \mathcal{K}_{j+1}(T, r)$.
nodes.title: Arnoldi vectors span the Krylov spaces

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
